seo.metaDescription: One value per category or period as bars, with a domain you control, a format preset, keyboard selection and a hidden data table.

props.markdown: One value per category or period, drawn as bars. `BarChart` takes your rows, the field for the x axis and the field for the value, and handles the scale, the tooltip, the keyboard and the screen reader.

Use `BarChart` to compare a single measure across a few categories (orders by region) or to show it over equally spaced periods (margin by week). Put the measure on `y`, set `format` once for the axis, the tooltip and the data table, and pass `domain` when a zero baseline would flatten the differences. For several series that share an x axis, [`LineChart`](/docs/line-chart) usually reads better; for a ranked list with long labels, use `RankedBars`.
Props stay serializable here, so the chart renders in a server component. `domain` keeps the bars from starting at zero, and `format="percent"` writes the axis and the tooltip.
With `onSelect` the chart needs a client component, because the handler is a function. Click a bar, or focus the chart and press `Enter`.

The chart is a single tab stop. Tabbing in shows the first bar with its tooltip and announces it. Arrow keys move between bars, `Home` and `End` jump to the first and last, `Enter` or `Space` selects the active bar when the chart has `onSelect`, and `Esc` clears the active bar. `Esc` is only consumed when a bar is active, so an enclosing dialog still closes.

Screen readers get the chart title and description, then an announcement for each bar the keyboard moves to, in the form “1 of 12, Jul 6, 37.5%”: the position, the label and the formatted value. A visually hidden data table with every value follows the chart, so browse mode can read it row by row.
The full model is in the [accessibility guide](https://github.com/mwadon/tally-charts/blob/main/docs/a11y.md).
